newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino journalist shot dead, wife wounded.
newsitem.headline: Filipino journalist shot dead, wife wounded.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead a veteran Filipino journalist and wounded his wife while the couple were chatting with relatives in front of their house near Manila, police said on Monday.

Alberto Berbon, the second journalist to die by an assassin's hand in the Philippines this year, was shot several times by two unidentified gunmen on Sunday evening in Imus town, Cavite province, police said. A stray bullet struck his wife.
Berbon, 45, was a senior editor at DZMM radio station of the multimedia network ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp,
Police said the two gunmen got out of a car and shot the journalist with an assault rifle and a pistol.
The gunmen, whom police said could be hired killers, escaped. The motive behind the killing was unknown.
The killing of weekly Press Freedom editor Ferdinand Reyes by a lone gunman in southern Dipolog city last February has not been solved.
More than 50 journalists have been killed in the Philippines in the past 20 years, many of them during the martial law regime of late president Ferdinand Marcos.
